protocol: D-000 adversarial review, turn 2 of 3 (reviewer side). Mandate: refute, not confirm. Every landing claim verified against bytes, none taken from the coordinator's report.
verdictSummary: Narrowed to 1 SHOULD-FIX + 1 NOTE, with 7 of 9 turn-1 items RESOLVED-VERIFIED in bytes and 2 PARTIALLY landed. The restructure is substantively right: the identity clause now matches the pinned stableId model with the two-custody adaptation honestly disclosed, the namespace clause states the pin's actual root-flat/declarative-sub-grammar shape, the alias window is decided in defined units here, and the alternatives block records the real alternatives with the prior misdescription acknowledged in place. The two residuals are small and mechanical; expectation of CONSENT at turn 3 is RECORDED, conditional only on their landing. One process finding: the coordinator's turn-2 message claims 'the file-08 annotation enumerates what is and is not decided' — the bytes do not; the annotation enumerates only decided items, omits transfer-in-class from that list, and names no deferral. Reports must trail bytes (the lane's own standing discipline, OBS-T3-01/OBS-D005-T3-01).

perItemStatus.note: Clause 1 realigns to the pin's author-declared immutable UUID (stableId) and supplies the missing enforcement as host-registry custody: two records (manifest declaration + persisted admission registry) with a uniqueness constraint, retired-ID retention, never-derived-from-mutable-state, names/aliases resolving through the ID. The PROJECT-ID-V1 citation now claims the two-record shape 'adapted to author-supplied identity' — the departure from caller-may-not-supply is named in place, which is what the fidelity standard requires. The rejected host-minted alternative is recorded with the portability ground. See OBS-2/OBS-3 for two non-blocking wording residuals.

Clause 2 states the pinned model: flat host-owned ROOT; declarative, host-interpreted sub-grammar (CommandSpec/parent) below a mounted root; no raw root parser authority; collision refusal over name, alias, or parent linkage. The Alternatives block now rejects STRICT flatness on the correct ground (the pin itself mounts declarative sub-grammar) and acknowledges the previous block's misdescription.

The DR-111 borrow is struck as an undefined-rule citation and the number is decided in this entry: at least one minor release cycle AND no fewer than 90 days from the deprecating release, whichever is longer. Self-contained; no forward reference remains, so no supersession clause is needed — any future DR-111 command-surface widening would itself be a reviewed act that can supersede this entry explicitly. See OBS-4 on whose release train 'minor release cycle' counts.

Clause 3 restores the static host-reserved root-command list by ADR-0159 shape citation (which carries visible + internal names and the implicit help), forbids claim or alias of a reserved name, and puts the CI parity test in the negative-test evidence; clause 7 separately tests reserved-name claim and parent-linkage collision.

Clause 4 decides scope precedence: same component at project+global resolves by the DECLARED order project-shadows-global with required disclosure — deterministic by declared scope order, distinguished from forbidden ordering-dependence. Different-ID name claims remain clause-2 refusals (clause 4's carve-out is scoped to 'a component admitted at both scopes', singular). The pin's warn-first-wins is the recorded alternative, rejected on the corpus's explicit-over-quiet ground.

Clause 6 corrects the class to first-party/EXPLICITLY-TRUSTED (D-002's actual words), gives transfer within the class a rule (registry bookkeeping under host authority with the two-custody update discipline — so the explicitly-trusted external-publisher case is governed, not assumed away), and makes the routing consistent: depth + third-party transfer/dispute to the DR-117 successor owned by DR-010; DR-116 the support/vulnerability side. See OBS-3 for the provenance-binding residual.

Clause 7's negative-test enumeration adds ID/version distinctness and multi-version coexistence (file 05's goldens class), parent-linkage collision, reserved-name claim, and the scope-precedence disclosure; the bounding quote carries 'stable IDs distinct from versions and aliases' and clause 1's immutability supplies cross-release constancy. The release-identity FIELD (file 02's 'component/release identity' pair) is still unnamed in clause 1 — absorbed into OBS-2's wording pass; non-blocking because the distinctness rule is bound, stated via immutability, and tested.

objections.claim: The accepted annotation-honesty item (T1-09) landed only half: the file-08 annotation enumerates decided items but names no residual — and its decided list is itself inaccurate. The coordinator's turn-2 message states the annotation 'enumerates what is and is not decided'; the bytes do not.
objections.evidence: Measured at register digest 03f0f919…, entry lines 1111-1115: the annotation reads 'identity, namespace, reservation, scope-precedence and alias policy DECIDED (D-012), sub-grammar ownership recorded; negative-test evidence at qualification.' Two mismatches: (1) ownership TRANSFER within the slice-1 class IS decided (clause 6's two-custody bookkeeping rule) but is absent from the decided enumeration; (2) nothing in the annotation names what is NOT decided or where it went — the deferral of namespace depth and third-party transfer/dispute to the DR-117 successor (owned by DR-010) lives only in the entry body. The lane's precedent is exact: D-007's DR-118 annotation carries 'PER-ROW THRESHOLDS REMAIN UNDECIDED' in the row itself, and turn-1 T1-09 — accepted, per the coordinator 'none rebutted' — asked for precisely the residual naming. A row reader must not need this register entry to learn the row's undecided half (the D-002 NOTE-10 principle: no scope exists only inside a register entry).
objections.proposedFix: Amend the planned row annotation to: 'identity, namespace, reservation, scope-precedence, alias-window and in-class transfer policy DECIDED (D-012); namespace depth and third-party transfer/dispute DEFERRED to the DR-117 successor (DR-010-owned), DR-116 carrying support/vulnerability; negative-test evidence at qualification.' One line; lands with C-D012.

objections.claim: The turn-1 NOTE's second half did not land: restoring the fourth bounding element ('no implicit execution during discovery') is done, but the policy still nowhere states that reservation/collision detection is computed from authenticated manifest metadata only, and clause 7's negative-test list has no execution-during-discovery/admission probe.
objections.evidence: The amended preamble carries the full four-element bound (lines 1056-1059). No clause states the metadata-only computation rule (clause 2's 'manifest discovery never hands a component raw root parser authority' is about grammar authority, not about executing code to compute reservations), and the clause-7 enumeration (collision, cycle, shadow, stale-alias, parent-linkage, reserved-name claim, scope-precedence disclosure, ID/version distinctness, multi-version coexistence) contains no no-execution probe. The pin's mechanism is explicit that this property is load-bearing: the reserved list is 'static so the admission gate needs no mounted program' and the manifest is inspectable 'without importing the runtime module.'
objections.proposedFix: One sentence in clause 7 (or 2): 'reservation and collision detection are computed from authenticated manifest metadata only; executing component code during discovery/admission is itself a refusal, with a negative test at qualification.' May land with the T2-01 edit in the same commit.

observations.text: Clause 1's 'the HOST enforces GLOBAL uniqueness at admission against its persisted admission registry' overstates what a per-install registry can enforce: registry custody yields install-local uniqueness; cross-install uniqueness rests on UUID randomness (statistical) plus signed provenance. Suggest 'uniqueness within the host's admission registry' or an explicit statement of the statistical assumption. Same pass can name the release-identity field (file 02's component/release identity pair) in clause 1. Non-blocking wording; suitable for the C-D012 change record or a turn-3 touch-up.

Clause 1's 'a retired ID is ... never readmitted for a DIFFERENT component' and clause 6's transfer discipline both need a discriminator for 'same vs different component' that cannot be the ID alone; the natural one is the signed publisher provenance the admission evidence already requires (file 02 §Common component packaging; DR-G08's install-trust surface in D-002's gate set). Stating 'custody binds ID to signed publisher provenance; transfer is a provenance rebind under the two-custody discipline' would close the loop the turn-1 fix proposed. Non-blocking: the two-custody rule is decided; this names its key.

Clause 5's 'one minor release cycle' does not say whose release train counts — the renaming COMPONENT's own minor releases (natural under file 04's anti-lockstep independent releases) or the distribution core's. The 90-day absolute floor makes the ambiguity non-blocking, but the qualification harness will need one reading; name it in the C-D012 change record.

The coordinator's turn-2 message reported the T1-09 annotation as landing 'what is and is not decided'; the bytes enumerate only the decided half (inaccurately — see T2-01). This is the report-ahead-of-bytes class the lane has now recorded three times (D-002 OBS-T3-01, D-005 OBS-D005-T3-01/T3-01); 'edits land before messages send' is standing discipline and applies to landing claims item-by-item, not only to digests.
